narrative.overview:
The product should feel like opening a soft lavender letter under gentle light: frosted glass, quiet gold seals, and cinematic animation as a primary craft pillar. It is intimate and mobile-first — never a dark luxury landing page, never a purple-glow dashboard, never generic stock romance, never a static brochure with a fade slapped on.

Depth comes from atmosphere (blurred abstract wash + aurora + sparse particles), glass cards, soft plum shadows, and layered motion. Motion must feel intentional and emotional: staggered word reveal, breathing logo, shimmer on the gift CTA, morphing date gate, sparkle/confetti unlock, scene-to-scene transitions, and interactive feedback. Always honor prefers-reduced-motion. /animate, /delight, and motion polish are default expectations.
keyCharacteristics: Animation-forward: every scene ships with purposeful entrances, transitions, and micro-interactions
Motion Contract binding: signature moment + supporting layers required before Done
Light Soft Lavender Mist canvas (not near-black)
Champagne gold as rare accent (dividers, seal, success)
Frosted glass cards with gradient edge

rules.name: The Mist-Not-Midnight Rule
rules.body: Do not use near-black full-bleed page backgrounds or the retired burgundy/gold palette.

rules.name: The Rare Gold Rule
rules.body: Champagne gold appears on ≤ a few ceremonial moments per screen (divider, seal, success). It is not a second brand purple.

rules.name: The Letter Body Rule
rules.body: Scene 1 letter paragraphs use --text-primary (#3a2440) with Alexandria so optical weight stays readable; do not lighten body to muted mauve for softness.

rules.name: The Atmosphere-Behind-UI Rule
rules.body: Blur and particles stay behind interactive content; never obscure text contrast.

rules.name: The Alive-Gift Rule
rules.body: A scene is incomplete if content is correct but motion is missing, generic, or only a single opacity fade. Each scene needs at least one memorable motion moment plus calm supporting motion.

rules.name: The Calm-Not-Chaotic Rule
rules.body: Motion supports reading and emotion; it must not fight the letter body, block taps, or feel like a marketing landing-page gimmick reel.

rules.name: The Reduced-Motion Rule
rules.body: Honor prefers-reduced-motion: skip infinite loops, shimmer, confetti, and heavy exits; keep clear layout and instant (or near-instant) content visibility.

rules.name: The Motion Contract Rule
rules.body: A scene is not Done until the Motion Contract checklist passes: entrance, content reveal, scroll reveal where relevant, one signature moment, interaction feedback, calm ambient, exit/transition, plus reduced-motion path. Animate transform/opacity only; no animated backdrop-filter; ≤1 signature + 2–3 supporting per viewport.

rules.name: The Card Enrichment Rule
rules.body: Any content card needs at least 3 of: category chip, watermark icon (opacity ~6–10%), type accent, icon/illustration, gradient edge. Champagne gold only for ceremonial moments.

dos: Do keep Soft Lavender Mist tokens in src/index.css as the code source of truth.
Do use Aref Ruqaa for display moments and Alexandria for body/UI.
Do design and ship animation as a core deliverable for every scene (entrances, transitions, interaction feedback).
Do pass the full Motion Contract checklist before requesting owner approval.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion (skip particles loops, shimmer, confetti, heavy exits).
Do build mobile-first; verify every scene on a phone-width viewport — motion must stay smooth on phone.
Do keep Soft Lavender Mist tokens, glass cards, and pill CTAs consistent across every scene.
donts: Don't invent personal photos, chats, or copy — placeholders must read as placeholders.
Don't put the engagement date in the logo.
Don't add a background music track or autoplay any audio.
Don't use near-black full-page backgrounds or the old burgundy/gold world.
Don't overload the first viewport with stats, schedules, or multi-card marketing grids.
Don't treat motion as optional polish after done — unfinished animation means unfinished scene.
Don't ship a scene with only a single opacity fade and no signature moment.
